title: 26 - Selling Poseidon
summary: At a remote session of Earth's survivor delegates, [[character:riker]], present through an avatar, trades barbs with [[character:ambassador-gerrold|Ambassador Gerrold]] over the failure to stop the attacks. He reports that the destroyed [[technology:kudzu-gardens|farm donut]] will take a few months to replace and the farm must be regrown, so rations will be short but no one will starve, and he publicly belittles [[organization:vehement]] as merely lucky, as bait to provoke it, while Guppy monitors every communication. The emigration debate goes nowhere: the Maldives and Micronesia have nearly secured [[location:eta-cassiopeiae-3|Poseidon]] but cannot recruit the six hundred more colonists they need, and others want the unfinished colony ships for Vulcan or Romulus. Guppy finds one anomalous tight-beam signal, sent from a remote part of New Zealand to [[character:homer]]; recalling how withdrawn and humourless Homer has become, Riker suspects he is helping the attackers, or is not Homer at all, and asks Charles to meet in person.

updates.current_state: He told the delegates the destroyed farm donut needs months to replace, with short rations meanwhile, and is baiting [[organization:vehement]] by downplaying it while monitoring all communications. A tight-beam signal to [[character:homer]] makes him suspect Homer is aiding the attackers or is not Homer, and he has asked Charles to meet.

He has stopped joking entirely and withdrawn from the other Bobs, very unlike himself. An anomalous tight-beam signal from a remote part of New Zealand was sent to him, and [[character:riker]] suspects he may be helping the attackers or may not be Homer at all.

At the remote delegates' session he again accuses [[character:riker]] of being unable to stop the attackers, seeming to enjoy the situation more than his anger suggests, and Riker, tired of his jibes, now answers back.

updates.state: The Maldives and Micronesia have largely cemented their claim to settle it, helped by other enclaves' lack of interest in so specialized a world. They still need about six hundred more colonists for a full colony-ship complement and are struggling to recruit them.
